public_rationale: Zitron said he did not believe OpenAI had 'any other viable options' for existing compute outside Microsoft. Reuters reported that OpenAI finalized a deal in May 2025, after months of talks, for Google Cloud to supply additional capacity to its existing infrastructure. Google Cloud is an operating provider, not a future build. OpenAI's supplier list soon named Google, Oracle and CoreWeave besides Microsoft. So at least one existing outside option was viable enough for OpenAI to use within weeks of the post. In fairness to Zitron, Google itself was short of capacity, and nothing shows these options could cover all of OpenAI's expansion. If 'viable' means fully sufficient, the claim cannot be checked.
limitations: Sources are anonymous-source news reports. Deal size was not disclosed.
The result depends on reading 'viable options' as usable existing capacity, not capacity sufficient for all expansion needs.

our_interpretation: This is stated as a belief about the situation at the time of the post. It is graded as a claim that, around April 2025, no provider other than Microsoft had existing (already built) capacity OpenAI could practically use to add compute.
Future builds (Stargate, CoreWeave's contracted 1.3 GW not yet built) do not count as existing. Contracts for capacity that is already built and supplied soon after the post do count.
Target period is Q2 2025, the quarter of the post. Arrangements closed within weeks of the post show which existing options were available then. This is flagged as a choice.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that around April-June 2025 OpenAI could not get meaningful additional existing capacity from any provider other than Microsoft.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that around April-June 2025 OpenAI arranged or used existing cloud capacity from a provider other than Microsoft to meet its growing compute needs.

evidence.excerpt: Google's cloud unit, which will supply additional computing capacity to OpenAI's existing infrastructure for training and running its AI models
evidence.explanation: Google Cloud, an existing provider outside Microsoft, agreed in May 2025 to supply OpenAI with additional compute. The same article says the deal had been under discussion for months, so this option existed when the post was written.

evidence.excerpt: Google already lacked sufficient capacity to meet its cloud customers' demands as of the last quarter
evidence.explanation: This partly backs the spirit of Zitron's point. Even the alternative providers were capacity-constrained, so how much Google could add is unclear.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI has included Alphabet’s (GOOGL.O) Google Cloud among its suppliers to meet escalating demands for computing capacity
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's own supplier list later confirmed Google Cloud, along with Oracle and CoreWeave, as compute suppliers. It falls just after the target period, so it is context.

evidence.excerpt: partnering to extend the Microsoft Azure Al platform to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) to provide additional capacity for OpenAl.
evidence.explanation: Oracle's existing infrastructure already supplied OpenAI before the post, but through Microsoft's Azure arrangement. It is ambiguous whether that counts as 'outside of Microsoft', so it is context only.
